reason: The vacuity is real and I proved it, but the finding is wrong about its own counterfactual and its fix would turn the gate red on the correct surface, so it is refuted with the corrected fix carried. WHAT CHECKS OUT. interaction-check.mjs:534 is `Number(early.record) < Number(late.record) || early.lastBar < late.lastBar`, and the right-hand disjunct is a term of line 532's own test that the entrance runs. Driven in chromium at 1440x960, ?state=full&v=light&motion=play, with the gate's exact sampling (200ms, then +2000ms): early={hero:28,lastBar:0,record:'0'}, late={hero:31,lastBar:168,record:'1'}. I re-ran the block with `.record` forced to `animation:none;opacity:1;clip-path:none` injected at DOMContentLoaded - the previous best painted from the first frame, before a single column, the exact inversion the assertion names - and line 534 still passed, because early.lastBar 0 < late.lastBar 168 carries it alone. Line 534 is also the only assertion in the file that touches the record's ordering (the other `.record` hits are 524/530 sampling, 638 label overlap, 660-668 record-tag-never-paints, 1063-1067 degraded state, 1436 skeleton visibility). So the headline stands: the assertion cannot fail for its own claim. WHY IT IS REFUTED ANYWAY. (1) The finding's stated counterfactual is false when driven. It claims that removing the 1.1s animation-delay would make the left disjunct go false. It does not: with `.record{animation-delay:0s}` the 0.6s draw is still mid-flight at the 200ms sample, so early.record=0.877 < late.record=1 and the LEFT disjunct is true too. The only counterfactual that actually isolates the vacuity is the no-animation one above, which the finding does not name. (2) The proposed fix is wrong against the real source and would fail the shipped, compliant surface. Its arithmetic is right - `.bar` is `grow 0.5s` at `calc(var(--i)*40ms + 340ms)` (lately.html:255-256), so the twelfth column runs 780-1280ms - but its threshold is not. `.record` is `draw 0.6s` at `animation-delay:1.1s` (lately.html:303) over `@keyframes draw{from{opacity:0}to{opacity:1}}` (line 518), so at 1280ms the record is already ~30% through its own fade: measured 0.849 at t=1294ms, and a poll loop that waits for the twelfth column's height to stop changing actually lands at ~1399ms where opacity reads 0.966. The fix requires that frame to be under 0.5. It would go red on a surface whose choreography is exactly right, which is a worse fault in a gate than the vacuous assertion it replaces. (3) The fix's premise is also slightly off: the record does not begin after the columns finish - it starts at 1100ms while the twelfth column is still growing to 1280ms - so any assertion phrased as 'record starts after the last column ends' fails on the master too. What is true, and is what the choreography actually claims, is that no part of the old ceiling is visible while the columns are being drawn (opacity is exactly 0 until 1100ms, with the twelfth column already at 162.6/168px by 1043ms) and it completes after they have all settled. SEVERITY. The seat's `defect` is the right class for the underlying vacuity - nothing on screen is wrong, the choreography measures correct, and what is missing is the guard - so I do not correct it upward; but the finding as filed does not earn a change because acting on it as written breaks the gate.
breaks: The replacement reads the animation timeline, so it is only valid inside the ?motion=play context - under ?motion=settled and prefers-reduced-motion the surface sets `animation-duration:1ms !important; animation-delay:0ms !important` (lately.html:536, 542) and every ordering collapses; keep it in the existing play block and do not lift it into the settled paths. It is coupled to three literals in the stylesheet - `grow 0.5s` / `--i*40ms + 340ms` (255-256) and `draw 0.6s` / `1.1s` (303) - so any retune of the entrance must be re-run against it, though it tests the relation rather than the numbers, which is the point. `animationName` matching depends on the keyframe names staying `grow` and `draw`; if either is renamed the find() returns undefined and the Boolean() guard fails loudly rather than silently, which is the correct failure direction. `getComputedTiming().delay` returning a number is Chromium behaviour and this gate is chromium-only, so that is safe here. After it lands, re-run the full interaction-check (461 assertions) and confirm the count rises by two and nothing in the record-tag-never-paints block at 660-668 or the skeleton visibility check at 1436 moves; nothing on the surface changes, so no frames need recapture and audit.mjs is untouched. Do NOT adopt the filed fix's opacity-under-0.5-at-settle probe: measured, the shipped surface reads 0.849 at the twelfth column's 1280ms end and 0.966 at the frame a poll loop actually catches, so it would make a green gate red.
